data.name: Bahir
data.gender_notes: Bahir is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who illuminates, the one who brings light, the one who shines brightly. The name Bahir carries the meaning “Radiant, Shining, Clear, Bright” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu. Parents who choose Bahir usually hope their child will grow to embody radiant, shining, clear, bright and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for the one who embodies the divine light, the one who shines forth with the light of God's guidance
data.etymology: Bahir belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Radiant, Shining, Clear, Bright.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bahir total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.long_meaning: باهر هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي، مشتق من الفعل 'بَهَرَ' الذي يعني الظهور أو البروز. يوحي الاسم بالشيء الذي يظهر أو يتجلى بوضوح، وقد يكون له دلالات على الشخص الذي يتميز بالظهور أو الشهرة. في اللغة العربية، الاسم باهر يستخدم لوصف الشخص الذي له تأثير واضح أو حضور قوي.

in_urdu.name: باہر
in_urdu.meaning: ظاہر یا واضح کرنے والا، مشہور
in_urdu.long_meaning: باہر ایک مذکر نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے ظاہر یا واضح کرنے والا۔ یہ نام اسلامی ثقافت میں اہم سمجھا جاتا ہے کیونکہ یہ ان خوبیوں کی نمائندگی کرتا ہے جو ایک فرد کو قابل ذکر بناتی ہیں۔

in_hindi.name: बाहिर
in_hindi.long_meaning: बाहिर एक पुरुष नाम है जो अरबी से आया है। इसका अर्थ है स्पष्ट या प्रसिद्ध करने वाला। यह नाम उन गुणों को दर्शाता है जो किसी व्यक्ति को विशिष्ट बनाते हैं। इस्लामी परंपरा में, यह नाम महत्वपूर्ण माना जाता है क्योंकि यह एक व्यक्ति की विशिष्टता को दर्शाता है।

in_english.name: Bahir
in_english.long_meaning: Bahir is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, derived from the verb 'bahara', which means to appear or to shine. The name signifies someone who is manifest, apparent, or has a shining personality. In Islamic tradition, Bahir is considered a significant name as it reflects the qualities that make an individual notable or distinguished. Etymologically, it relates to the Arabic root 'B-H-R', which conveys the idea of appearance or emergence.

historical_references.reference: Bahir al-Din al-Umari was an Andalusian scholar and theologian. He was born in Granada in 1174, and studied under Ibn Rushd (Averroes). Bahir al-Din is best known for his work 'Al-Burhan fi'l-Tasawwur', a commentary on Avicenna's 'The Book of the Causes of Things'. He died in 1248.
historical_references.context: Andalusian scholar and theologian, student of Ibn Rushd (Averroes), known for commentary on Avicenna's 'The Book of the Causes of Things'.

historical_references.reference: Bahar al-Din al-Zarkari was a Persian Sufi of the Chishti order. He was born in 1182 in Herat, in present-day Afghanistan. He traveled widely throughout the Islamic world and was a spiritual guide to many, including Amir Khusraw, a famous poet and musician. Bahar al-Din died in 1262 in Multan, Pakistan.
historical_references.context: Persian Sufi of the Chishti order, born in Herat, spiritual guide to many, including Amir Khusraw, died in Multan.
